nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.text: Afternoon! Careful, the pavement's hot enough to fry an egg on today. Not that I've got any eggs. Or anything, really.

nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.text: Back again? Still nothing in the freezer, I'm afraid.

nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.text: What can I do for you?

nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.text: I do! Well. I'm supposed to. I've been out all summer. Every morning I open the freezer and it's just... cold air. Funny, isn't it?

nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.text: Nobody's complained. Nobody ever seems to want any. You're the first person who's asked in... huh. I don't actually know how long.

nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.text: Isn't it? It's always like this here. Every single day. I honestly can't remember the last time it rained.

nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.text: ...Ha. Sure, hon. Aren't we all?
Her smile stays exactly where it is, for a moment too long.

nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.text: Oh! Oh, where did you— no. Never mind. Don't tell me. It's perfect.

nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.text: It's cold. It's actually cold. Thank you. I think I'd forgotten what the cart was for.

nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.text: You again! I'm still thinking about that cone. Don't tell anyone, but it's the best thing that's happened around here in ages.

nodes.speaker: Old man
nodes.text: Mind the pigeons. They think they own this bench. They may well be right.

nodes.speaker: Mr. Halvorsen
nodes.text: Back for more pigeon wisdom?

nodes.speaker: Mr. Halvorsen
nodes.text: Sit, if you like. There's room.

nodes.speaker: Mr. Halvorsen
nodes.text: Halvorsen. Arne, if we're going to be friends. My wife used to call me 'Arne the Bench'. She thought she was very funny. She was.

nodes.speaker: Mr. Halvorsen
nodes.text: Every day. I sit, I feed them, I watch the sun go down. Well. The sun doesn't really go anywhere, does it? Hm. Never noticed that before.
He stops throwing crumbs.

nodes.speaker: Mr. Halvorsen
nodes.text: The real world. I don't think I've ever been. Have you?

nodes.speaker: Mr. Halvorsen
nodes.text: Four. Eleven. Eleven. Twenty-three. Thirty. Forty-one.
The pigeons have stopped moving.

nodes.speaker: Mr. Halvorsen
nodes.text: ...Why would you ask me that?

nodes.speaker: Mr. Halvorsen
nodes.text: I'd rather just sit for a while, if it's all the same to you.

nodes.speaker: Kid
nodes.text: Hey! HEY. Look how high it is! It's the highest one ever. Probably.

nodes.speaker: Theo
nodes.text: It's still up there! I'm Theo, by the way. I already told you that. Did I?

nodes.speaker: Theo
nodes.text: Wanna hold the string? You can't, actually. It's mine.

choices.text: Who's that man down the street? The dark one.
None of this is real. I'm dreaming.

nodes.speaker: Theo
nodes.text: I know! I made it go up there just by wanting it to. You can do that here, you know. You just have to really, really want it.

nodes.speaker: Theo
nodes.text: Somewhere. Mom says I can stay out till the streetlights come on.

nodes.speaker: Theo
nodes.text: They never come on, though.

nodes.speaker: Theo
nodes.text: What man?

nodes.speaker: Theo
nodes.text: There's nobody there. You're being weird.

nodes.speaker: Theo
nodes.text: No you're not.

nodes.speaker: Theo
nodes.text: ...Don't say stuff like that. It makes the sky go weird.

nodes.speaker: Theo
nodes.text: I'm not talking to you. You say weird stuff.

barks: Can't stop! I'm on lap... I forget which lap!
Morning! Or afternoon. Whatever it is!
Same loop every day. Never gets old!

nodes.speaker: The phone
nodes.text: ...Hello? Oh, thank goodness. It's Mina, love. From the cart. By the fountain?

nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.text: I've been ringing every phone in the city. You went such a long way.

choices.text: How did you get this number?
How do I get out of here?

nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.text: You gave it me. Don't you remember? You said, ring if it ever rains. It's raining, love. It hasn't stopped since you left.

nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.text: Somewhere very big and very empty, by the sound of it. You always did wander off too far.
A long silence on the line. Rain, somewhere behind her.

nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.text: Real? I sell ice cream to people who never eat it. ...Don't ask me things like that. It makes the line go funny.

nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.text: Out the back, there's a way down. Stairs. Now listen: don't you take your eyes off them. Things out there don't like being looked at - but while you're looking, they can't go anywhere.

nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.text: And come back to the park, after. Everyone's waiting for you. Even the man who doesn't move. Especially him.
The line clicks. Then a dial tone. Then nothing at all - not even the dial tone.

nodes.speaker: Mr. Halvorsen
nodes.text: Oh. You found the garden. Hardly anybody finds the garden. Sit, if you like. The pigeons don't mind.

nodes.speaker: Mr. Halvorsen
nodes.text: It's very quiet here. That's the point of it, I think.

choices.text: The man who doesn't move. Do you know him?

nodes.speaker: Mr. Halvorsen
nodes.text: Somewhere for the ones who aren't needed any more. When a dream's over, the people in it have to go somewhere. Most of us end up here. It's not a bad place. There's a bench.

nodes.speaker: Mr. Halvorsen
nodes.text: I'm not sure I was ever alive, to be honest with you. I was the old man on the bench. That was the whole of me. ...It was a good bench.
He throws a crumb. The pigeons don't move for it.

nodes.speaker: Mr. Halvorsen
nodes.text: You know who's in Ward 6. You've been visiting every night. You sit by the bed, and you never stay long enough to see who wakes up.

nodes.speaker: Mr. Halvorsen
nodes.text: Him. He was in your city. And your yellow rooms, and your water, and up on your roofs. He's very tired, I think. Carrying all of it about, for you.

nodes.speaker: Mr. Halvorsen
nodes.text: He never did anything to anyone, you know. He only ever stood where you were most afraid. Someone has to.

nodes.speaker: Mr. Halvorsen
nodes.text: The gate, at the far end. It goes somewhere none of us have been. The middle of it all, they say. The pigeons found this in the grass - I think it's yours.
He puts an old iron key in your hand. It's warm, as if he'd been holding it a long time.

nodes.speaker: Mr. Halvorsen
nodes.text: Mind how you go. And if you see the summer again... say hello to the bench for me.

nodes.speaker: Mr. Halvorsen
nodes.text: Go on. The gate. I'll be here. I'm always here.
